approach: The game's x86_64 macOS binary or its 32-bit Windows binary (Learn & Play) is statically recompiled to C at build time and compiled for arm64; small native libraries replace Steam, Bink, Cg and the Intel-only parts, and Win32 and Direct3D 9 for the Windows binary.
help: Testing on other Apple Silicon Macs, especially 120 Hz ProMotion displays
Audio interfaces and inputs other than the Real Tone cable
Bug reports from long play sessions, DLC and custom songs
Play testing of Learn & Play, which has had far less of it than the Mac game
notes: Native arm64 builds for Apple Silicon Macs, no Rosetta at run time, from either of two games: the Steam macOS game, and Learn & Play, an edition Steam offers for Windows only. Each builds from your own Steam copy with an installer; ships no game code. Offline by design (every non-local connection is refused). Both render through the project's own GL-on-Metal layer, Learn & Play's Direct3D 9 included; the Mac game keeps Apple's OpenGL as a choice and the fallback. The frame rate follows the display (75/120 Hz); the Mac game takes about a sixth less CPU than the original under Rosetta, Learn & Play about as much as it. Songs, DLC, custom songs, Session Mode and lessons work in both.
